lint failure seems to be in the base branch only

> Nice feature!
> 
> There's no tests of the `infiniteHits` widget using the `cache` option, but only a unit test for `createInfiniteHitsSessionStorageCache`, which is a specific implementation of the cache.
> 
> In order to test the widget in a closer way of a user implementation, can we add a higher-level test for `infiniteHits` with a manual implementation of `cache`?

@francoischalifour thanks for the feedback. What kind of test are you expecting? Tests on widget level? or e2e test?
I didn't particularly add widget-level tests, because anyway I have to mock either sessionStorage or localStorage, then it becomes almost the same as the in-memory cache implementation. 

Maybe I can write a test where I provide a cache to an InfiniteHits instance, and take the cache and create another InfiniteHits instance with the cache to see if it properly renders all the hits without search request. What do you think?

What you could do is an integration test that follows these steps:

1. Add `infiniteHits({ cache: customCache })` where the custom cache implements the documented interface
2. Search stuff...
3. Go back to a previous state
4. Make sure that the cache is read

Would that make sense?

@yannickcr alright, thanks!
I'll try with that way.

Okay this was quite tough.
It was impossible to test the cache behavior of InfiniteHits with "pagination" widget, because whenever page changes, connectPagination refined the search. And that's not the behavior we want to test.

So I added two integration tests.
The first one is a basic test checking if `read` and `write` methods of the cache are being called correctly.

The second one is more similar to what I manually tested on the example website.
It creates a `instantsearch()` instance and add InfiniteHits. It "loads more" to the second page.
Now we have the hits of the two pages in the cache.

With that cache, we create another `instantsearch()` instance and see if the InfiniteHits widget correctly displays the whole hits from the cache.

What do you think?
Yes you'll have to re-create a PR, but you can re-use this branch for it.
@eunjae-lee thanks for the confirmation, though strange it works for you (my setuP MacOS 10.13.6, Chrome 85.0.4183.121) - looks like I've resolved it as shown, all good now!
